items.title: Burnham pledges early intervention and ‘benefits backstop’ to tackle youth jobs crisis
items.desc: Prime minister promises ‘root-and-branch rethink’ of support for young people as Milburn report advises sweeping changes to some benefits Andy Burnham: The crisis facing Britain’s young people is politicians’ fault. To fix it, we need a generational response Andy Burnham has pledged to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”. Burnham said the government would intervene at all the stages of life in which young people fell behind, and “long before they find themselves out of work and reliant on the state”, including providing more opportunities for vocational training in schools. items.title: Andy Burnham to say Brexit ‘has not worked’ and he will sign new deal with EU
items.desc: Prime minister is to meet European leaders at summit this week and secure agreements that ‘could raise GDP by 0.4%’ Andy Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit “has not worked” and that he will sign a new deal with the EU. It is the latest in a string of comments by the prime minister criticising Brexit, after he told the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday that the UK has “lost more than we gained” through leaving the EU. Is consistent with the Labour manifesto and the government’s red lines. It improves the Brexit deal and brings it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016. items.title: Digital finance products used to abuse almost 20% of young women and girls, UK report finds
items.desc: Survey respondents describe current or former partners controlling bank accounts and taking out credit online without full consent Almost one in five young women and girls in the UK have experienced digital financial products being used as a tool of abuse by a current or former partner , a report has found. Abusers are exploiting banking apps, online payments and digital credit to control young women, causing financial harm and preventing them from leaving relationships, according to research from the charity Surviving Economic Abuse. In the UK, call the national domestic abuse helpline on 0808 2000 247, or visit Women’s Aid . In the US, the domestic violence hotline is 1-800-799-SAFE (7233). In Australia, the national family violence counselling service is on 1800 737 732. Other international helplines may be found via www.befrienders.org Continue reading...

items.title: ‘Loaded with potential’: stage version of TV smash It’s a Sin has the dancefloor at its heart
items.desc: Exclusive: Trailer released for Rambert’s version of Russell T Davies’s show about friendship amid the 80s Aids crisis and the ‘extraordinary freedom’ of clubbing Russell T Davies’s award-winning series It’s a Sin, about young gay friends living through the Aids crisis in 1980s London, is getting a new life as a dance piece , with a trailer released on Monday ahead of an opening at Aviva Studios in Manchester in February. “We had a few approaches, but a lot of people wanted to make it a musical, which made my heart sink slightly,” said Davies. “I always imagined an aria between those two women on the seafront at the end and I thought: ‘Oh, that could be so terrible!’” Dance was different, he said. “It felt so original and so pure. The story distils down to these emotional moments that are going to be done so beautifully on stage.” Continue reading...
